summary: Rewrote the 'How Drop7 works' learn page (web/content/learn/rules.mdx) as a complete animated rulebook: board and pieces, player view / information boundary, drops and legal columns, the exact-run clearing rule (row, column, mismatch, gray discs counting), cracking, revealing and double hits, gravity and chains, scoring curve and bonuses, the five-drop rise, and both game-over conditions, ending in a one-table rulebook. Added web/scripts/generate-rules-scenarios.ts, which plays every scenario through the TypeScript engine in latent mode and writes web/content/learn/rules-scenarios.json, so all animated boards are engine output; and web/components/Rules.tsx (RulesScenario playback with HUD and static filmstrip, DropPhysics, RunCounter, RiseClock, ScoreCurve, PlayerView, LegalColumns, DiscLegend). Added a 'How Drop7 works' guide card and GitHub repository links (https://github.com/keshavsaharia/drop7-bench) to the console homepage, header and footer. Fixed a pre-existing renderer defect: next-mdx-remote's default blockJS stripped every JSX expression prop from MDX.
validationPerformed: cd web && npm run rules:scenarios; cd web && npx tsc --noEmit; cd web && npx eslint on changed files; cd web && npm run build; rendered /learn/rules, /, /learn via next start + curl and inspected full-page chromium screenshots
limitations: Self-reported contribution; not yet independently reviewed.
